name: Gu Kailai
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; she entered Peking University around age 20 after the gaokao was reinstated and was still completing her LLB/MA studies at age 26. She qualified as a lawyer and founded her law firm in 1988 at age 30.
early_history_summary: Gu Kailai was the youngest daughter of General Gu Jingsheng, a prominent revolutionary. During the Cultural Revolution she was forced to work in a butcher shop and textile factory. After the gaokao was reinstated, she entered Peking University, earning an LLB and then an MA in international relations.
family_context_summary: Youngest of five daughters of General Gu Jingsheng, a prominent revolutionary who was imprisoned during the Cultural Revolution; mother was a descendant of Song dynasty chancellor Fan Zhongyan.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a Communist Party general; family was part of the 'princeling' red aristocracy, but Gu suffered during the Cultural Revolution when her father was imprisoned.
evidence_summary: Gu Kailai came from a prominent revolutionary family but suffered during the Cultural Revolution, working in a butcher shop and textile factory. She entered Peking University after the gaokao was reinstated, earning law and international relations degrees. Her legal career began in 1988 at age 30 when she founded the Kailai Law Firm, well after age 26.

name: Jee Seok-jin
milestone_by_age_26: Released his debut album 'I Know' as a singer in 1992 at age 26, marking his entry into the entertainment industry.
early_history_summary: Jee Seok-jin graduated from Ajou University with a business administration degree before pursuing entertainment. He debuted as a theater actor in 1985 at age 19 and as a musical actor in 1988, before releasing his first singing album in 1992. The album had underwhelming commercial performance but launched his entertainment career.
family_context_summary: Born in Jeongseon County, Gangwon Province, South Korea; attended Ajou University for business administration. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Jee Seok-jin began performing as a theater actor at 19 and expanded into musicals and music before his 1992 debut album. His close friend Kim Yong-man encouraged him to pursue comedy after the album underperformed, leading to his KBS comedian recruitment in 1993. His career is characterized by persistence and versatility across singing, comedy, and hosting rather than early advantage.
starting_point: Born in Jeongseon County, Gangwon Province, South Korea; attended Ajou University for business administration; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Veteran cast member of SBS Running Man since 2010; one of the longest-running variety show personalities in Korean television.

trajectory.event: Debuted as a theater actor, beginning his performing arts career.
Released debut album 'I Know' as a singer, marking his entertainment industry debut.
Passed KBS 10th generation comedian recruitment exam, pivoting to comedy.
Became main MC of Star Golden Bell, which aired from 2004 to 2010 and established his broadcasting reputation.
Joined cast of SBS Running Man, which became a globally popular variety show.

name: Ong Teng Cheong
milestone_by_age_26: No material career milestone by age 26 found; he graduated with a Bachelor of Architecture from the University of Adelaide in 1961 at age 25 and was working as an architect in Adelaide, but his significant career milestones (joining Ministry of National Development, founding his firm, entering politics) all came after age 26.
early_history_summary: Ong Teng Cheong was born in Singapore and entered school late due to the Japanese Occupation. He studied architecture at the University of Adelaide on his father's friends' help, graduating in 1961, then worked as an architect in Adelaide before receiving a Colombo Plan scholarship for a master's in urban planning at the University of Liverpool in 1965.
family_context_summary: Second of five children from a middle-class Singaporean family; father's friends helped him travel abroad for education.
evidence_summary: Ong Teng Cheong came from a middle-class Singaporean family and graduated with a BArch from the University of Adelaide at 25. He worked as an architect in Adelaide but his material career milestones — joining Singapore's Ministry of National Development in 1967, founding his architectural firm in 1971, and entering politics in 1972 — all occurred after age 26.

name: Sam Michael
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Team Lotus in Formula 1 in 1993 at age 22 as a data acquisition and lap simulation engineer, entering the pinnacle of motorsport engineering.
early_history_summary: Sam Michael grew up in Canberra, Australia, and studied mechanical engineering at the University of New South Wales, writing his thesis on data acquisition systems for racing cars. During his studies he worked part-time for Greg Siddle on Mark Larkham's Formula Holden car. After graduating in 1993, he was recruited by Peter Collins to join Team Lotus in Formula 1.
family_context_summary: Born in Western Australia, grew up in Canberra; studied mechanical engineering at University of New South Wales. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: hands-on motorsport during studies, data acquisition thesis, mentor via Greg Siddle, F1 recruitment
evidence_summary: Sam Michael combined university engineering study with hands-on motorsport work, writing his thesis on racing data acquisition and working part-time for Greg Siddle's Formula Holden team. This practical specialization led to his recruitment by Team Lotus in Formula 1 at age 22. His data acquisition expertise was a scarce skill in early 1990s F1, and his direct domain immersion during studies accelerated his entry into the sport's highest level.
starting_point: Born in Western Australia, grew up in Canberra; studied mechanical engineering at University of New South Wales; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Executive Chair and Co-Founder of Ox Mountain, applying machine learning to maintenance automation; advisor to Triple Eight Race Engineering; formerly Sporting Director at McLaren and Technical Director at Williams F1.

trajectory.event: Joined Team Lotus in Formula 1 as a data acquisition and lap simulation engineer after graduating from UNSW.
Joined Jordan Grand Prix after Lotus bankruptcy, establishing the team's R&D department with a seven-post rig and active differential.
Promoted to race engineer at Jordan, working with Ralf Schumacher and then Heinz-Harald Frentzen, achieving race wins.
Promoted to Technical Director of Williams F1, responsible for all technical aspects of the race car.
Joined McLaren as Sporting Director, overseeing racing, testing, and driver operations.
Left Formula 1 and transitioned to machine learning and automation with Ox Mountain.

name: Manolo el del bombo
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; he became famous as a football superfan starting with the 1982 FIFA World Cup at age 33, with his first abroad trip to watch Spain in 1979 at age 30.
early_history_summary: Manolo el del bombo was born Manuel Cáceres Artesero in Ciudad Real, Spain, and raised in Huesca. He became Spain's most famous football supporter, recognizable by his large beret, red number 12 jersey, and bass drum. His fame began at the 1982 World Cup in Spain and he attended all of Spain's international matches from 1982 onwards.
family_context_summary: Born in Ciudad Real, Spain; raised in Huesca. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Manolo el del bombo became famous as a football superfan but his celebrity status emerged at the 1982 World Cup when he was 33. No evidence of any material milestone by age 26 was found in reviewed sources; his early life before his football fandom career is largely undocumented.

name: Khun Sa
milestone_by_age_26: Formed a militia band in his home area of Loi Maw in 1950 at age 16, initially serving Kuomintang forces and later raiding their outpost to seize rifles, launching his military career in the Golden Triangle.
early_history_summary: Khun Sa was born Zhang Qifu in a remote village in Northern Shan State, Burma. Orphaned by age 5 (father died at 3, mother shortly after), he was raised by his Han Chinese grandfather, the village headman. He received no formal education but had military training from Kuomintang soldiers. At age 16, he formed a militia band, demonstrating early tactical opportunism in the chaotic post-WWII Burma borderlands.
family_context_summary: Orphaned by age 5; father was a Chinese soldier who died when Khun Sa was 3, mother died shortly after. Raised by his Han grandfather, who was the village headman of Loi Maw.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a soldier from Yunnan, China; grandfather was village headman with local authority. No formal education was provided.
primary_early_advantage_tags: orphaned, no education, Golden Triangle geography, Kuomintang military training, survival-driven
evidence_summary: Khun Sa was orphaned by age 5 and raised by his grandfather in a remote Golden Triangle village, receiving no formal education. The chaotic post-WWII borderlands created a power vacuum that an opportunistic teenager could exploit. At 16 he formed a militia band, leveraging Kuomintang military training and his geographic immersion in the opium trade corridor. His extreme adversity and frontier geography were the dominant forces shaping his early path.
starting_point: Born in a remote village in Northern Shan State, Burma; orphaned by age 5, raised by his Han Chinese grandfather who was the village headman; no formal education.
current_position: Died October 26, 2007 at age 73 in Yangon, Myanmar; final role: retired drug lord and warlord who surrendered to the Burmese government in 1996 and engaged in legitimate business.

trajectory.event: Formed a militia band in Loi Maw, initially serving Kuomintang forces and later raiding their outpost to seize rifles.
Turned his Kuomintang unit into a private army and entered the drug business, building his own heroin laboratories.
Engaged in the 'Opium War' with rival Kuomintang officers, consolidating power in the Golden Triangle.
Assumed the Shan name Khun Sa and became the dominant opium warlord, controlling a large share of Golden Triangle heroin.
Surrendered to the Burmese government, disbanded his army, and moved to Yangon with his wealth.
Died in Yangon, Myanmar.

name: Rob Halford
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Judas Priest as lead vocalist in May 1973 at age 21, and recorded debut album Rocka Rolla in 1974 at age 23, launching what would become one of the most iconic careers in heavy metal.
early_history_summary: Rob Halford grew up on the Beechdale housing estate in Walsall, West Midlands. He was a good singer from childhood, featured in school nativity plays. Before music took over, he worked as a glass engraver and at a local cinema. He was singing in local bands including Hiroshima when his sister Sue, who was dating Judas Priest bassist Ian Hill, introduced him to the band. He joined in May 1973, bringing drummer John Hinch with him.
family_context_summary: Grew up on the Beechdale council estate in Walsall, West Midlands; working-class background. Childhood friend of Noddy Holder (later of Slade) who also lived on the estate.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family musical background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: extraordinary vocal range, West Midlands metal scene, sister connection to Ian Hill, working-class council estate
evidence_summary: Rob Halford grew up on a working-class council estate in Walsall with no documented family musical background, but possessed an extraordinary vocal range noticed from childhood. The West Midlands was an emerging hub for heavy rock in the early 1970s. His sister's relationship with Judas Priest bassist Ian Hill provided the critical network connection. Halford had been performing in local bands since his late teens before joining Judas Priest at 21, where his vocal talent and the complementary team dynamics created one of metal's most iconic lineups.
starting_point: Born in Sutton Coldfield, grew up on the Beechdale council estate in Walsall, West Midlands; working-class family with no documented musical background.
current_position: Lead vocalist of Judas Priest, still actively touring and recording; net worth approximately $14 million; released album Invincible Shield in 2024 with tours scheduled through 2026.

trajectory.event: Joined Judas Priest as lead vocalist, playing first show in May 1973 at the Townhouse in Wellington, Shropshire.
Made recording debut on Judas Priest's first album Rocka Rolla.
Released British Steel, Judas Priest's mainstream commercial breakthrough album.
Released Painkiller, cementing legendary status; subsequently left Judas Priest to form Fight.
Rejoined Judas Priest after an 11-year hiatus.
Won Grammy Award for Best Metal Performance with Judas Priest.
Inducted into Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Judas Priest.

name: Ernesto Valverde
milestone_by_age_26: Made his professional debut with Deportivo Alavés in the Segunda División in 1982 at age 18, launching a 14-year professional playing career.
early_history_summary: Ernesto Valverde was born in a small village in Extremadura but moved to the Basque Country as an infant. He joined the San Ignacio youth system (1975-1981) and then the Alavés youth and amateur setup, making his professional debut with Alavés in 1982. He progressed through Sestao and then Espanyol, where he made his La Liga debut in 1986 and reached the UEFA Cup final in 1988, before transferring to Barcelona.
family_context_summary: Born in Viandar de la Vera, Cáceres, Extremadura; moved to the Basque Country as an infant. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: youth system from age 11, Basque football culture, professional debut at 18, La Liga progression
evidence_summary: Valverde moved to the Basque Country as an infant and entered the San Ignacio youth system at age 11, progressing through Alavés youth and amateur teams to make his professional debut at 18. The Basque Country's strong football culture and youth development pipeline provided the ecosystem for his early career. He reached La Liga with Espanyol by 22 and a UEFA Cup final by 24, demonstrating steady progression through Spain's football pyramid.
starting_point: Born in a small village in Extremadura, Spain; moved to the Basque Country as an infant; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Head coach of Athletic Bilbao (third spell, 2022-2026); announced in March 2026 he would step down at end of season; most successful manager in club history with record 451+ matches and a Copa del Rey title in 2024.

trajectory.event: Made professional debut with Deportivo Alavés in the Segunda División.
Made La Liga debut with RCD Espanyol on 31 August 1986.
Part of Espanyol squad that reached the UEFA Cup final, then transferred to FC Barcelona.
Joined Athletic Bilbao, becoming the club's top scorer with 16 goals in his first season.
Became head coach of Athletic Bilbao, launching his managerial career.
Appointed manager of FC Barcelona, winning La Liga and Copa del Rey double in 2017-18.
Won Copa del Rey with Athletic Bilbao, the club's first major trophy in 40 years.

name: Nirmal Purja
milestone_by_age_26: Became the first Gurkha to join the UK Special Boat Service (SBS) in 2009 at age 25, one of the most elite special forces units in the world, before his mountaineering career began.
early_history_summary: Nirmal Purja was born in a poor village in Nepal's Myagdi District. His father was a Gurkha soldier and his mother from a farming background; their inter-caste marriage led to family cutoff. Three older brothers became Gurkhas and funded his English-speaking boarding school education. He joined the Brigade of Gurkhas in 2003 and was accepted into the SBS in 2009, becoming the first Gurkha in the elite unit. His mountaineering career began later, in 2012.
family_context_summary: Born to a poor family in Dana village, Nepal; father was a Gurkha soldier, mother from farming background. Parents' inter-caste marriage led to social and financial cutoff from both families. Three older brothers became Gurkhas and funded his education.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father and three older brothers were Gurkha soldiers, providing a direct military career pathway and funding for his boarding school education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Gurkha family tradition, brothers funded education, SBS selection, extreme poverty, inter-caste stigma
evidence_summary: Purja's path was shaped by extreme poverty and family military tradition. His father and three older brothers were Gurkhas, providing both a career template and funding for his education. The Gurkha recruitment pipeline and subsequent SBS selection represented an elite performance pipeline that few achieve. His inter-caste family background created significant adversity that likely fueled his drive. The SBS milestone at 25 demonstrated exceptional physical and mental endurance before his mountaineering fame.
starting_point: Born to a poor family in Dana village, Nepal; father was a Gurkha soldier, mother from farming background; parents cut off from families due to inter-caste marriage; grew up without basic necessities.
current_position: World-record-holding mountaineer, MBE; founder of Elite Exped; pursuing 'Hat-Trick Challenge' to summit all 14 eight-thousanders for a third time; 50th summit of an 8000m peak achieved in July 2025.

trajectory.event: Joined the Brigade of Gurkhas in the British Army.
Became the first Gurkha to pass selection for the UK Special Boat Service (SBS), the elite special forces unit.
Summited Mount Everest for the first time.
Completed Project Possible, climbing all 14 eight-thousanders in 6 months and 6 days, a world record.
Led the first winter ascent of K2 without supplemental oxygen, the last great mountaineering prize.

name: Takaaki Kajita
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; he joined the Kamiokande experiment as a graduate student in 1981 at age 22 but his Ph.D. was completed in 1986 at age 27 and his first paper on atmospheric neutrinos was published in 1988 at age 29.
early_history_summary: Takaaki Kajita grew up in a small city north of Tokyo and studied physics at Saitama University, where he spent considerable time on Japanese archery. He joined Professor Masatoshi Koshiba's group at the University of Tokyo as a graduate student in 1981, working on the Kamiokande experiment. He completed his Ph.D. for proton decay search in March 1986 and began studying atmospheric neutrinos, which eventually led to his Nobel Prize-winning discovery of neutrino oscillations in 1998.
family_context_summary: Born in Higashi-Matsuyama, a small city about an hour north of Tokyo; grew up in a peaceful countryside environment surrounded by rice fields. Family background not detailed in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Kajita joined the Kamiokande experiment as a graduate student under future Nobel Laureate Masatoshi Koshiba in 1981 at age 22, but his first significant research output — his Ph.D. — came in 1986 at age 27. His first paper on atmospheric neutrinos was published in 1988, and his Nobel Prize-winning discovery of neutrino oscillations came in 1998 at age 39. No material milestone by age 26 was identified.

name: Robert Kalina
milestone_by_age_26: Was employed by the Austrian National Bank in 1976 at age 21 as its sole engraver, selected while still a Vienna art student to succeed Austria's official money designer, a highly specialized and scarce position.
early_history_summary: Robert Kalina studied at the Graphische Lehr- und Versuchsanstalt (Federal Training and Research Institute of Graphic Arts) in Vienna. While still a student, he was selected to succeed Austria's official money designer and was employed by the Austrian National Bank in 1976 as its only engraver, a pupil of Roman Hellmann. He went on to design all Austrian Schilling banknotes from 1982 and won the 1996 competition to design the euro banknotes.
family_context_summary: Born in Vienna, Austria on June 29, 1955. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: national bank selection, engraving apprenticeship, Vienna art school, sole engraver position
evidence_summary: Kalina was selected while still a Vienna art student to become the sole engraver at the Austrian National Bank at age 21, an extraordinarily scarce position in currency design. He trained at the Graphische Lehr- und Versuchsanstalt and was a pupil of Roman Hellmann at the National Bank. This institutional pipeline — from art school to national bank — provided direct domain immersion in currency design and access to specialized engraving facilities that few designers in the world possessed.
starting_point: Born in Vienna, Austria; studied at the Graphische Lehr- und Versuchsanstalt (Federal Training and Research Institute of Graphic Arts); family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Designer at Oesterreichische Banknoten und Sicherheitsdruck GmbH since 1998; known worldwide for designing the euro banknotes that entered circulation in 2002 across 12 EU countries.

trajectory.event: Employed by the Austrian National Bank as its sole engraver, selected while still a Vienna art student.
Designed his first Schilling banknote (ATS 1000 featuring Erwin Schrödinger).
Designed the ATS 5000 banknote featuring Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.
Won the European Union's euro banknote design competition, chosen from 44 entries.
Euro banknotes entered circulation across 12 EU countries, making his work one of the most widely seen designs in history.

name: Dan Shomron
milestone_by_age_26: Served as a squad commander in the 1956 Sinai Campaign at age 19, participating in combat operations as a paratrooper in the IDF's elite Paratrooper Brigade.
early_history_summary: Dan Shomron was born in Kibbutz Ashdot Ya'akov in 1937. He enlisted in the IDF in 1955 at age 18 and volunteered for the Paratrooper Brigade, assigned to Battalion 890. He served as a squad commander during the 1956 Sinai Campaign, then completed the Infantry Officers Course and served as a platoon commander. He briefly left the military in 1959 to work as a truck driver on his kibbutz before re-enlisting in 1962 as a company commander.
family_context_summary: Born in Kibbutz Ashdot Ya'akov, Mandatory Palestine; eldest of three children of Tova and Eliyahu Dozorets-Shimron. Grew up in a kibbutz collective farming community.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; kibbutz background provided a communal, militarized society context.
primary_early_advantage_tags: kibbutz upbringing, IDF paratrooper pipeline, frontier state, combat at 19, Sinai Campaign
evidence_summary: Shomron grew up in a kibbutz in the Jordan Valley, immersed in Israel's frontier-state militarized culture. He enlisted at 18 and volunteered for the elite Paratrooper Brigade, seeing combat as a squad commander in the 1956 Sinai Campaign at 19. The constant military conflict of early Israel provided direct domain exposure and an elite institutional pipeline. His kibbutz background meant no financial advantage but deep communal and national security immersion.
starting_point: Born in 1937 in Kibbutz Ashdot Ya'akov, Mandatory Palestine; eldest of three children in a kibbutz collective farming community in the Jordan Valley.
current_position: Died February 26, 2008 at age 70 in Herzliya, Israel; final role: 13th Chief of Staff of the IDF (1987-1991), later Chairman of Israeli Military Industries.

trajectory.event: Enlisted in the IDF and volunteered for the Paratrooper Brigade, assigned to Battalion 890.
Served as squad commander during the Sinai Campaign, participating in combat operations.
Commanded a unit on the Egyptian front in the Six-Day War, becoming the first paratrooper to reach the Suez Canal; awarded Medal of Distinguished Service.
Commanded the 401st Armored Brigade in the Yom Kippur War, crossing the Suez Canal and fighting in Egypt.
Planned and commanded Operation Entebbe, the daring hostage rescue at Entebbe Airport in Uganda.
Became the 13th Chief of Staff of the IDF, serving until 1991.
Died in Herzliya after a stroke.
